data.description:
## Why
In the c11 1.0 run, staging to Atlas was slow all day and caused real stalls. `scripts/remote_build.py` caches bundles by SHA, but every new head creates `parent-<head>.bundle` from `git bundle create ... HEAD`, which carries the full history (about 170 MB). The Hyperion to Atlas link measured about 160 KB/s (2026-10-02 15:51). With ten seats staging at once, seats hit their 900 s command cap (15:00), Atlas load reached 54, and a captain gate waited behind uploads (12:20). The workaround was to build and run guests on Atlas and never ship built apps across the link.

## Done when
- A remote build for a new head uploads only the objects Atlas does not have: an incremental bundle against a base the host already holds, or a `git fetch` on Atlas from the forge.
- Staging a head whose parent Atlas already has takes seconds, not minutes, measured over the Hyperion link.
- `tests/test_remote_build_routing.py` (or a sibling test) covers the incremental path and the fallback to a full bundle when no shared base exists.

Source: c11 1.0 run retro, `.lattice/orchestration/c11-1.0/run-state.md` entries 12:20, 15:00 and 15:51 on 2026-10-02.
data.title: Remote builds upload only what Atlas lacks, not a full-history bundle per head

data.body:
PR #587 (https://github.com/Stage-11-Agentics/c11/pull/587), head 05fe7671bf.

Design: the build host keeps one bare mirror per repository (parent, ghostty, vendor-bonsplit). The client asks which heads each mirror holds and bundles HEAD minus everything reachable from them. With no shared base it falls back to a full bundle; with the head already held it sends no bundle. The host fetches the bundle into its mirror (git checks the prerequisites), verifies the mirror ref equals the requested SHA, and checks out that exact ref; the existing identity checks are unchanged. A new mirror adopts the heads of existing per-tag checkouts. Submodules use the same path, replacing the SHA-keyed bundle cache.

Evidence:
- tests/test_remote_build_routing.py: 11 pass; the 4 new tests (base selection plus incremental path, full-bundle fallback, far-side prerequisite refusal, migration adoption) error against the old script.
- Real runs to Atlas, Debug, no launch, tag c11-331:
  - 37bb4ad (parent had no cached seed): old path 176.7 MB full bundle, 404.8 s upload. New path: incremental parent bundle only, staged in 13.5 s, including one-time mirror creation.
  - 05fe767 (parent held): old path 2.0 MB rsync delta plus an 8 s local 176 MB bundle, 14 s. New path: a 778 B bundle, 0.03 MB payload, staged in 5.0 s; build plus retrieval 39.8 s. C11_REMOTE_OK, and the Atlas checkout HEAD equals the requested head.
- The c11-hotload skill describes the staging; not synced (sync after merge).

Repair r1 pushed at bdea994aac. 1) Mirror init, publication and verification now run under one flock per repository mirror, shared by the held-heads probe and mirror_head; the exact-SHA check is kept, and a failed fetch is an error. 2) A mirror that is not a bare repository is rebuilt (init plus adoption in a staging dir, then rename); the probe now runs the same script on the host from stdin, and a host failure fails staging. New tests test_overlapping_requests_for_one_new_head_both_publish_it (deterministic: a reference-transaction hook pause plus an announced lock wait) and test_interrupted_mirror_initialization_is_rebuilt (parent and ghostty mirrors) are red on 05fe767 and green here; the suite is 13/13. Real Atlas run at bdea994: 0.04 MB staged in 6.0 s, C11_REMOTE_OK, and the Atlas checkout HEAD equals bdea994.

Review PASS at bdea994aac (Astra, round 2; r1 FAIL on concurrent mirror publication and incomplete mirror init, both fixed). PR #587 in draft, held until 1.0 releases; Cairn lands it, then syncs c11-hotload and clears the old ~/c11-builds/bundles cache on Atlas once no old-script run remains.
Astra review PASS r2 at bdea994aac; merged 4785de26f9 (#587); PR files identical in the merged tree; routing tests 13/13 at the merge state.
